{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the sales data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert 'revenue' to float, coercing errors to NaN
# But do NOT drop any rows — keep all 900 for the population
sales['revenue'] = pd.to_numeric(sales['revenue'], errors='coerce')

# Confirm the full population size
print("Total rows in full dataset:", len(sales))

# Compute conversion rate per customer_segment using ALL rows
# Conversion rate = sum(converted) / count(converted) per segment
# 'converted' is integer and fully populated, so no need to drop
# We do not use 'revenue' in this calculation

# Group by customer_segment and compute totals
total_per_segment = sales.groupby('customer_segment')['converted'].count()
converted_per_segment = sales.groupby('customer_segment')['converted'].sum()
conversion_rate = converted_per_segment / total_per_segment

# Print the raw counts and rates
print("Total customers per segment (full population):")
print(total_per_segment)
print("Converted customers per segment (full population):")
print(converted_per_segment)
print("Conversion rates per segment (full population):")
print(conversion_rate)

# Find the segment with the highest conversion rate
top_segment = conversion_rate.idxmax()
max_rate = conversion_rate.max()
print(f"\nHighest conversion rate: {top_segment} with {max_rate:.4f} ({max_rate*100:.2f}%)")

# Return the top segment name
print(top_segment)"}
